caption:
🗽 Lower and Midtown Manhattan, every building standing today by year of construction — 1850 → 2025.

Most of what stands here went up in one 50-year rush. Tenements for immigrants came first (1880–1910), then the first skyscrapers like the Flatiron (1902), then the Art Deco race of the Chrysler (1930) and the Empire State (1931). The Depression and WWII stopped almost everything for 15 years. After the war came housing projects and glass office towers, and One World Trade Center rose on the site of the Twin Towers.

📊 Data: NYC Open Data building footprints and PLUTO, with historians' dates from the Landmarks Preservation Commission where available. 59% have a precise year; 40% are city estimates rounded to the decade, often off by up to 20 years, spread over nearby years, so the 1900 peak is partly a rounding artifact. Heights exaggerated.
🌍 Map: OpenStreetMap contributors.
